grade.subject: docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S11-honest-instruments/stream1-design/design.md (rev 1, RECONCILED, 435 lines)
amendments: State explicitly what 'conforms' means for a clause whose subject matter does not exist on a given surface (no identity concept, no aggregate, no parseable input) — an explicit vacuous-pass state, not silence.

State a decidable procedure (or an explicit, reasoned heuristic) for enumerating the population of 'reporting surfaces' subject to the contract, since T1's lint 'walks the reporting surfaces' presupposes this set is already known.

Extend the seven clauses' inspection procedures to cover document/prose reporting surfaces (status files, dashboards) or explicitly scope them out with a reason — the inspection language currently presupposes a programmatic declaration.

Correct §1's claim that both arms 'independently reject' a two-valued Option/Maybe, an out-of-band status field, and a nullable record — only arm B (T859) raises and rejects those three; arm A (T857) never mentions them.
grade.decidability_table_summary: 7 clauses x 3 real repo surfaces (bin/managent orient's lane-count line at src/managent/main.zig:7075-7079; managent done's verdict/flag resolution at src/managent/main.zig:4706-4746 and :3553-3568; S11's own STATUS.md state labels). Clean decidable fails: C1/C2 on orient's count and done's verdict, C3 on done's verdict, C5/C6 on STATUS.md labels. Clean decidable pass: C4 on orient's count, C5 on done's model-attribution gate. Needs interpretation: C1/C2 on STATUS.md (prose-citation-vs-structured-field ambiguity); every N/A cell across all three surfaces, because the contract never states whether a clause whose subject doesn't exist on a surface counts as pass, skip, or undecidable.
grade.non_vacuity: Constructed and confirmed two failing surfaces already present in this repository: (1) `managent done T900 --verdict fail-found ...` silently drops the unrecognised --verdict flag and defaults verdict to pass (src/managent/main.zig:3560, :4740-4746) -- fails clause C3, and is independently named as a live gate condition in the T857/T859 briefs that produced the graded design's own source arms; (2) readResumeFloor (src/managent/main.zig:6380-6404) defaults missing JSON keys to 0, indistinguishable from a genuine floor of 0 -- fails C1's fabrication rule; currently latent (all keys present in tools/hooks/claimlint-floor.json as of 2026-08-24) but the code path is real. Sibling type ClaimlintSummary in the same file uses optional fields to avoid exactly this, five lines away.
grade.cost_honesty: S6/S7 traced against both arm documents in the untracked working tree (not cited by path here, same reason design.md gives); nothing found dropped. One cost neither arm nor the reconciliation names: migration cost for external, non-type-system consumers (shell scripts grepping today's bare-value stdout/JSON) when a surface's wire format changes shape -- distinct from the caller-branches-three-ways cost already named, which is about in-process callers.
grade.reconciliation_integrity: Spot-checked 5 of section 5's choices (5.1 staleness, 5.2 vacuous check, 5.3 provenance, 5.4 identity, 5.5/5.6 caller-rule and known-broken-register) against both arm documents in full -- all five accurately state which arm contributed what and why, nothing dropped without mention. One inaccuracy found outside section 5 but bearing on the same integrity question: section 1 claims both arms 'independently reject' a two-valued Option/Maybe, out-of-band error codes/status field, and a nullable record; only arm B (T859) actually raises and rejects those three (its section 2, numbered list) -- arm A (T857) never mentions any of them. Only the fourth item, confidence-valued readings, is independently stated by both arms. Silence presented as independent convergence overstates the evidence the document uses to argue trivalence is 'the shared root'.
grade.fitness_for_stream3: Not writable as-is. Beyond the four amendments, the document nowhere specifies how to enumerate/bound the population of 'reporting surfaces' a comparison would score -- section 4's T1 lint presupposes that set is already known. Combined with the N/A-clause ambiguity and the prose-surface gap, three reviewers would draw the surface boundary differently and score the same repository differently, which is the defect this grade exists to catch. None of this requires redesigning the mechanism -- each amendment is a sentence-scale addition.
